q: Momentum (p) of a body is defined as the ____, which is written as $p=mv$.
c: product of the mass of the body and its velocity
e: Momentum quantifies the amount of motion an object has, depending on both its mass and speed.

q: Momentum of a body is ____ to its velocity.
e: For a given mass, an increase in velocity results in a proportional increase in momentum.
Because velocity is a vector, momentum also has both magnitude and direction.

q: Direction of momentum is the same as that of ____.
e: Since mass is a positive scalar, the momentum vector points in the exact same direction as the velocity vector.

q: Unit of momentum is expressed as the ____.
c: product of mass unit and velocity unit
e: The unit of momentum is derived directly from its definition as mass times velocity.
Kilogram meter per second is the standard SI unit for momentum.

q: One fundamental law of physics is the ____.
e: This law states that the total momentum of an isolated system remains constant if no external forces act on it.

q: This law states that: If there is no net external force acting on an ____, the total momentum of the system is constant.
e: An isolated system is one that does not interact with its surroundings, meaning no external forces are applied.

q: The law of conservation of momentum is a general law and is true for both ____ objects.
e: Conservation of momentum applies universally, from colliding billiard balls to subatomic particle interactions.

q: According to law of conservation of momentum, ____ = total momentum after collision.
e: In any collision within an isolated system, the sum of momenta before the event equals the sum of momenta after.
